subject: Routing options for procurement: cloud marketplace listing vs direct contract (FinSight pilot)
messages:

Cc: procurement@finsight.ai

Subject: Routing options for procurement: cloud marketplace listing vs direct contract (FinSight pilot)

Hi Karthik,

We're lining up procurement for a short pilot (3 months, up to 50k tokens/day) and wanted to understand tradeoffs between purchasing via AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace vs going direct with Redwood. A few practical questions from our side: 

- Which route gets us to a PO/invoice faster (typical calendar days)?
- If we go marketplace, can we still get co-sell support from AWS (we may want joint outreach later)?
- Are pricing/discounts identical across marketplace vs direct? Any revenue-share implications we should be aware of?
- For compliance, what artifacts do you need to list on a marketplace (SOC2, contact for security review)?

We have an internal procurement constraint: for small pilots they prefer marketplace invoicing because it shortens legal review. But the product team wants the option to escalate to a direct contract if we want a longer-term engagement. Can you outline the recommended path and next steps?

Thanks,
Sarah Wong
Head of Platform Partnerships
FinSight Analytics

Subject: Re: Routing options for procurement: cloud marketplace listing vs direct contract (FinSight pilot)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear brief. High-level guidance below, plus a recommended two-step path that many pilots use. TL;DR: Marketplace is fastest to get you running; direct contract gives more predictable billing and negotiable terms if you expect to scale.

Marketplace (pros/cons)
- Pros: ~3–14 business days to buy once listing is live (depends on your procurement cadence), minimal legal review, simple vendor onboarding, consolidated invoice from the cloud provider.
- Cons: Slightly reduced flexibility on custom terms (MSA redlines), discounts are typically baked into marketplace pricing or via private offers; revenue share with the marketplace vendor is common (affects Redwood's net price) but pass-through pricing to you can be equivalent with a private offer.

Direct contract (pros/cons)
- Pros: Full control over MSA terms, SSO/KMS integrations, custom billing cadence (monthly or ARR), easier to configure reserved/dedicated capacity and SLAs.
- Cons: Procurement/legal review can add 2–6 weeks for a typical mid-market PO and longer if security questionnaires are involved.

Co-sell with cloud providers
- You can run on marketplace and still engage AWS/GCP/Azure co-sell teams via a private listing/partner lead process. Co-sell eligibility often requires a partner relationship and a case submission; the cloud team can help with introductions whether you entered via marketplace or direct.

Recommended two-step path for pilots (what we usually do)
1) Start on the marketplace for speed: Redwood issues listing and you purchase the pilot seat. We provide a 30–60 day runway and attach a simple SOW for usage expectations.  
2) Parallel: Redwood Ops & Legal share a trimmed MSA + SOC2 artifacts so your legal team starts review. If you decide to scale, we convert to a direct contract (use the already-reviewed MSA, exchange a PO, and set up invoicing).

Artifacts we normally need for a marketplace listing: SOC2 report (summary), product security contact, liability caps (we can provide standard language), and a short product listing description. I attached a one-pager that explains this flow and a quick checklist.

Next steps
- If that sounds good, can we schedule a 30-min sync with your procurement on Mon/Tue? I can bring Laura (revenue/partner ops) and Vanessa (cloud channel) who can answer co-sell and invoice routing specifics.

Attaching: Redwood_procurement_one-pager.pdf (one-page checklist)

Best,

Team — forwarding Sarah's note. Quick questions before the sync: 

1) Co-sell: For AWS, if we list on the marketplace and they request co-sell involvement later, do we need a private offer to preserve partner credit? And what lead time does AWS expect?
2) Discounts/private offers: If we offer a marketplace private offer (to avoid revenue-share leakage), do we still honor the same discount if customer converts to a direct contract?
3) Legal: for a 3-month pilot are we okay providing the SOC2 summary + standard MSA stub, or should we push for a short SOW instead?

My inclination: recommend marketplace purchase to unblock procurement, run parallel MSA review. Vanessa, can you confirm typical marketplace listing timeline for AWS and whether we can attach a private offer (and how that affects co-sell eligibility)? Laura/Vivek, any constraints on backstopping billing/credits if they convert mid-pilot?

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Fwd: Routing options for procurement: cloud marketplace listing vs direct contract (FinSight pilot) -- quick internal question

Karthik / team — quick answers from channel ops: 

1) Co-sell & private offers: For AWS the recommended pattern is to create a private offer (aka private pricing) on the marketplace — that preserves the marketplace purchase flow for the customer and allows the vendor (Redwood) to specify custom pricing. We then register the opportunity with AWS for co-sell. Lead time: 5–10 business days to create a private offer and register for co-sell; AWS approval for co-sell can add another 3–7 days.

2) Discount portability: If we provide a private offer on marketplace, we can make that pricing portable for a limited window when converting to a direct contract, but the accounting/bookkeeping needs a clean handoff. Laura, we'll need you to confirm revenue allocation rules if the deal moves from marketplace invoice to direct Redwood invoice mid-quarter.

3) Legal/artifacts: For a short pilot, SOC2 summary + standard MSA + a 1–page SOW is sufficient. Avoid heavy redlines at the start. We can accept marketplace purchase for immediate access and have Legal work the MSA in parallel for conversion.

I'll join the sync. I can also pull the AWS co-sell checklist and the DocuSign template for private offers.

Vanessa
Director, Channel Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: AWS_co-sell_playbook.pdf (PDF, 420KB)]
